newsitem.title: CHINA: Rain eases north China drought, temperatures cool.
newsitem.headline: Rain eases north China drought, temperatures cool.

text.p: Rain has eased a heatwave in drought-stricken northern China but state media warned on Friday that more hot weather was on the way.
Temperatures dropped by more than five degrees Celsius (41 degrees Fahrenheit) in north China on Thursday after two weeks of unseasonal sweltering.
Thermometers hit 40C (104F) in some places, the China Daily said.

The cold front since Tuesday had brought cloudbursts that dumped up to 300 mm (12 inches) of rain in some parts of the north, it quoted Tang Huifang, deputy director of the Central Meteorological Observatory, as saying.

Unusually high temperatures and low rainfall in areas north of the Yangtze River since June have threatened the autumn grain crop, with a record 20 million hectares (49 million acres) of arable land hit by drought.
More than 70 percent of China's grain is gathered in the autumn.
However, summer weather would return to normal in the next few days with the north entering the hottest period of the year between July 19 and August 18, Tang said.
"Hot summer days in northern China are not over yet," he warned.
Officials have said the drought in northern areas would affect this year's corn crop but would not cut the overall grain harvest below forecast levels of about 484 million tonnes for the year.
